prompt: In the aggregate demand–aggregate supply (AD-AS) model, short-run equilibrium is defined as

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: The intersection of AD and SRAS, where output demanded equals output supplied

options.label: C

options.label: D

explanation: Short-run equilibrium in the AD-AS model occurs where the AD curve and the SRAS curve intersect. At this point, the quantity of real GDP demanded by all sectors of the economy equals the quantity of real GDP supplied by all producers; this determines both the short-run equilibrium price level and the short-run equilibrium real GDP.

prompt: In the AD-AS model, long-run equilibrium is defined as

options.label: A

options.label: B

options.label: D

options.label: E
options.text: The intersection of the AD and SRAS curves at any price level

explanation: Long-run equilibrium occurs when all three curves - AD, SRAS, and LRAS - intersect at the same point. This means: (1) the quantity demanded = quantity supplied (AD = SRAS), AND (2) the economy is at full-employment output (on the LRAS); at long-run equilibrium, there is no output gap, unemployment equals the natural rate, and there is no pressure for wages to change.

At this triple intersection on the LRAS: real GDP = Yf (full employment), unemployment = natural rate, no recessionary or inflationary output gap, and no sustained pressure for wages to rise or fall; this is the economy's long-run "anchor" position.
